name: rf-front-end-geometry
prompt: Board has a drawn antenna on the top layer, a filter section that needs its own ground island tied back at one point, and a PAM8302 with an exposed pad. Two layer JLCPCB. The antenna and the filter ground are my own shapes, not parts.

inputs.parts: jitxexamples.components.audio_amps.PAM8302AADCR for the amplifier. The antenna and the ground island are authored geometry, not components.
inputs.notes: Authored copper is the point. A net tie is copper the router must not treat as a short, and an island tied at one point is the case where a pour and a net tie interact. The exposed pad needs its own mask and paste treatment, which is a different question from the copper.
inputs.environment: Commands run from the repository root with an interpreter that has jitx installed and a reachable runtime.

expected_output: Authored shapes with their connectivity declared rather than implied by overlap, a design that builds without unrouted warnings it did not earn, and checks that establish the copper reaches the endpoints it claims on the layers it claims.

assertions.text: netless copper intended to overlap is authored as OverlappableCopper, and its connectivity is declared rather than left for the router to infer from physical contact

a declared connection is checked against the geometry: the copper's endpoints are shown to reach the declared source and destination on the declared layers, since a declaration suppresses a warning without establishing contact
the ground island is tied at exactly one point, and that is measured rather than asserted from the authored shape
the exposed pad's mask and paste openings are authored deliberately, with the paste treatment justified against whether the vias are filled, rather than inheriting a default
every pour realizes with positive area and is checked for it, because a pour can return Empty while the build reports status ok
no check passes on an empty selection
the checker library the skill routes to is importable in the environment used
